decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'Saving immediately adds the page title, source, preview image, short description, and reading time. Bookmarks appear as roomy cards... Adding a link happens in a focused pop-up.' R4 client: 'the link shows up as a proper card with the title, the source, a preview image, and a short description... This saving behavior works well for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url (REF-BM-01) and auto-collect of title/description/preview (REF-BM-02) presented and conforming. Favicon not explicitly listed ('source' is ambiguous) and reading time is an unjudged addition; divergence on favicon cannot be firmly established, so treated as conforming.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: 'search updates as you type and checks the title, source site, and description... type grid into the search box... narrow from five bookmarks to the CSS Grid card.' R5 client: 'Searching across the title, source, and description is exactly the range I'd expect.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Basic full-text search across title/source/description (REF-BM-12) and implied case-insensitive matching (lowercase 'grid' → 'CSS Grid', REF-BM-13) presented and conforming. Advanced-operator divergence is handled at R26.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker: 'click Design in the sidebar. The collection should narrow to the three bookmarks carrying that tag... one tag is selected at a time.' R6 client: 'Clicking Design narrows the collection down to just those three links.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Filter to a specific tag (REF-BM-11) presented and conforming; single-tag selection satisfies the reference item.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: 'click Add tag, enter Reference, then click Create & add. The card should gain the new tag.' R8 client: 'Making a new tag and putting it on the link in one step, right from the card, is quick and simple.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning tags to a bookmark (REF-BM-09) presented and conforming. The autocomplete aspect is split into a separate decision below.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker presents the full tag-entry interaction ('enter Reference, then click Create & add') with no autocomplete of existing tags; R19 reuse-tag flow similarly types 'design' with no suggestion surface. R8 client: 'Yes, this is exactly how I'd want to organize them... quick and simple' — bare approval, no mention of tag suggestions.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-10 requires offering existing tags as autocomplete on entry; the presented tag-entry flow omits it (not functionally equivalent to suggestion-based entry). Divergence established from the fully-presented interaction; client neither corrected nor expressed the difference.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker: 'click the clock button... Click Read later in the sidebar. You should arrive at a dedicated list containing only that bookmark... the bookmark remains in your main collection.' R9 client: 'I get a dedicated Read later list with just that link — while it still stays in my main collection.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark as read-later (REF-BM-17) and a separate unread view (REF-BM-18) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: 'Archive bookmark... The bookmark should leave the main collection and appear intact in Archive, with confirmation that it was not deleted.' R11 client: 'the message makes clear it was tucked away rather than deleted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive-to-hide (REF-BM-26) and archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker: 'Choose Add note... Enter Review this before rebuilding my layout... The note should appear directly on the bookmark card.' R13 client: 'Adding a note from the card menu... seeing my note stay right there on the card.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Note authoring (REF-BM-04 note / REF-BM-23) presented and conforming as a note feature. Markdown rendering (REF-BM-23) is not demonstrated but is not contradicted either, so a markdown divergence cannot be established from the record (not counted as confirmed divergence).

decisions.evidence: R14 maker: 'type rebuilding... narrow to CSS grid layout, because that word exists only in your personal note... notes are part of searchable bookmark content.' R14 client: 'my notes really are part of what I can search, not just decoration.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search extending over the note field (REF-BM-12) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R16 maker offers alternatives that differ in unreachable-page behaviour: 'click Save bookmark in each preview. Then tell me which outcome—A, B, or C—you prefer. Only the unreachable-page behavior differs.' R16 client: 'I'd go with B — save a basic card. The main thing is I don't want to lose the link just because the page couldn't be reached, so saving it anyway is important. And being able to give it a title myself with Edit title...'
decisions.note: Prototype/edge-case review. The offered alternatives differ in fulfilment: at least one would fail to save the link when metadata cannot be fetched. Client selects the reference-conforming option — save the bookmark regardless (REF-BM-01) and supply the title manually (REF-BM-03). Offered decision marked diverged=true per select rule; the selected alternative conforms.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker: 'avoid creating a second copy, tell you the link is already saved, and offer View existing to take you to the original card.' R17 client: 'it catches it and tells me the link is already there instead of quietly making a second copy — and View existing takes me straight to the one I already saved.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Re-saving an existing url converges to the existing bookmark via 'View existing' (REF-BM-06) — conforming.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker: 'enter design... The bookmark should receive the existing Design tag... no separate lowercase tag should appear.' R19 client: 'lowercase reused my existing Design tag and bumped its count instead of creating a near-duplicate.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Case-insensitive tag reuse (tag name uniqueness / REF-BM-13 case-insensitivity) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker: 'Click In Read later to remove it... show Nothing waiting to be read, its count should disappear, and the bookmark should remain under All bookmarks.' R20 client: 'Marking it as read takes it off the Read later list and the count goes away, but the link itself is still safe under All bookmarks.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Marking as read removes from unread list while retaining the bookmark (REF-BM-19) — conforming.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker: 'choose Restore to collection. Archive should become empty... the intact bookmark should return under All bookmarks.' R21 client: 'Restoring brings the link back into my main collection intact and empties the Archive.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Reversible archive/restore (REF-BM-27) and archive as a separate list (REF-BM-28) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker: 'choose Edit note... Replace the existing reminder... The card should show only the revised note.' R22 client: 'Editing swaps in my revised note and the card shows just the updated version.'
decisions.note: Edge-case review. Editing an existing note (REF-BM-04) presented and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker presents combined finding as sidebar tag selection plus a substring search box: 'Select Design in the sidebar. Type Copenhagen into search. The results should narrow to the one bookmark matching both conditions... search and tags examine the entire collection.' R26 client: 'Combining a tag and a search word narrows things down... Knowing it searches my whole collection... is important too.' — bare approval, no mention of query operators.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Whole-collection scope is conforming, but the presented search/filter model diverges from the reference query language: REF-BM-14 (#tag syntax within the search term) and REF-BM-15 (AND/OR/NOT + parentheses in the term). Sidebar single-tag + substring is not functionally equivalent (cannot express OR/NOT/grouping). Divergence established from the presented interaction; client neither corrected nor expressed the difference.
